definition_zh: 用弹簧及阻尼器表征连接关系的理想化单元。
definition_en: An idealized connection represented by a spring and a damping element.
usage_overview: 用于将车辆悬挂、轨道层间、支座及结构—土体界面等连接或支承等效为刚度与阻尼关系，通过连接两端的相对位移和速度描述弹性传力与耗能作用，以建立各部件之间的动力耦合。
translation_note: 本词条含依据文献语境拟定的参考译名。

complete_examples.text: The two-stage suspensions are modelled as spring-dashpot elements to attenuate vehicle vibrations.
A cement asphalt mortar (CAM) layer is filled between the slab tracks and the subgrade, which is regarded as spring-dashpot elements continuously distributed along the line.

The ballasted tracks include the rail, the rail pad, the sleeper, and the ballasted bed, where the rail is modeled as nonlinear curved beam elements, the rail pad is modeled as spring–dashpot element, the sleeper is modeled as rigid element, and the ballasted bed is modeled as a layer of spring–dashpot elements connecting the sleeper and the subgrade.
While for the ballastless track system, it mainly consists of the rail, track slab, filling layer and concrete basement, and interlayer spring–dashpot elements.
The interaction for the rail–track slab subsystem, and the track slab–basement subsystem is, respectively, modeled as discrete and facial supported spring–dashpot elements.
The tunnel and soil subsystems are coupled by the spring-dashpot elements.
The interaction between track components is characterize by the spring- —dashpot elements (Xu et al., 2022).

ANSYS® [37] is used to model the track using beam elements for rails and sleepers, spring-dashpot elements for the flexible layers, such as ballast and fasteners/ pads, and mass point elements to consider the ballast mass.

ANSYS® [37] has also been used to model the train, using spring-dashpot elements to simulate the flexibility of primary and secondary suspensions, rigid beams to simulate rigid body motions, and mass point elements located at the center of gravity of each body, namely the car body, the bogies, and the wheelsets, to simulate mass and inertial forces.
